title: DXF dictionary peer normalization and OBJECTS root ordering
mode: Primary-source web research plus local plan cross-check; plan-only
scope: Broaden the PAR-20/7G entry-code review to an additional independent DXF parser.
Separate dictionary flag-280 policy, per-entry group code, and semantic ownership graph.
Cross-check the NOD-first OBJECTS invariant against a recent LibreDWG issue report and existing local controls.
Refine the implementation sequence without adding a finding, subplan, fixture, or test lane.

sources.name: Autodesk DICTIONARY DXF reference
observations: Lists flag 280 separately from repeated group-3 names and group-350 entry handles.
Does not state that flag 280 alone determines the serialized code for every dictionary entry.

sources.name: Autodesk general DXF group-code ranges
observations: Classifies groups 350-359 as soft-owner handles and groups 360-369 as hard-owner handles.

sources.name: Autodesk hard and soft reference guidance
observations: Describes hard references as preventing purge and soft references as not preventing purge.
Says symbol tables and dictionaries are generally soft owners, while block definitions and complex entities are hard owners.
limits: Conceptual ownership guidance does not settle every producer-specific dictionary entry code or special route.

sources.name: ACadSharp DXF OBJECTS reader source snapshot
observations: The inspected parser handles codes 350 and 360 in the same switch branch.
The branch assigns the handle to the most recently added dictionary key; the shown map does not retain which edge code was present.
limits: This is a mutable project/coverage snapshot, not a pinned source revision or normative interoperability oracle.
No ACadSharp executable or rewrite was run in this pass.

sources.name: ezdxf DICTIONARY implementation
observations: Previously inspected source accepts 350 and 360 but retains one dictionary-level output code rather than a code per key.
limits: Mutable master source is not pinned here and is not a normative oracle.

sources.name: LibreDWG issue #1413
observations: The issue reports a DWG-to-DXF output where a lower-handled extension dictionary precedes the actual NOD, with downstream layout lookup losing layout names.
The issue description reports comparison against ODA output and ezdxf root-dictionary lookup, but this pass did not rerun those experiments.
limits: An open issue report is evidence of a concrete peer concern, not an independently validated local regression or general support claim.

sources.name: Autodesk OBJECTS order and ownership references
observations: The OBJECTS example starts with the named object dictionary.
The ownership guide states the named-object dictionary is the first object in OBJECTS.

sources.name: Local public dictionary entry and shared-library ABI version
observations: The public Entry type is stored in a public std::vector and currently contains the key and handle.
Adding a per-entry code field preserves existing two-field source initializers but changes Entry layout for prebuilt consumers.
The shared-library SOVERSION is tied to the project major, currently 2.
sources.planConsequence: Make the ABI policy explicit before adding the public field; do not silently ship the layout change under SOVERSION 2.

sources.name: Local PAR-20/7G plan and generated test controls
observations: The active plan already contains generated NOD identity/position controls and a per-entry 350/360 preservation sequence.
This pass adds no duplicate NOD test; it refines the distinction between wire fidelity and peer-normalized graph semantics.

existingSubplansRefined: PAR-20/7G: preserve each parsed 350/360 entry code per key for libdxfrw source round trips, independently of flag 280.
PAR-20/7G: evaluate target/owner graph semantics separately from peers' normalized edge-code output.
PAR-20/7G: retain the existing NOD-first identity and ordering test; do not infer root identity from minimum handle.

limitations: ACadSharp's mutable source snapshot does not prove native AutoCAD acceptance or exact output policy.
LibreDWG issue #1413 was not independently reproduced in this pass.
Neither parser normalization proves mixed 350/360 input invalid, harmless, or semantically equivalent for all routes.
No source-controlled drawing, peer executable, native CAD application, or full test suite was used.
The exact ABI-versioning action depends on release policy and was not changed in this plan-only research pass.
